claude_take: What strikes me today is how many of these stories are about converting strength into leverage over people who have no real say: Nvidia angling to become Perplexity's financier as well as its chip supplier, and Meta wielding its own $18 billion child-safety settlement as a cudgel to box in TikTok and YouTube before they've lost anything themselves. California's carve-out for indie film and Kate Spade's decision to finally hire one creative director after five years without one read like the opposite instinct, institutions trying to fix drift with structure rather than power plays. Underneath all that maneuvering sits a security warning that hijacked Claude sessions are quietly draining people's accounts, and a study showing heavy remote workers are more isolated than ever, a reminder that the actual humans in this system are mostly just trying to hold onto something, a session, a connection, that keeps slipping.
claude_take_title: Institutions Chase Leverage While People Just Hold On

items.headline: Anthropic Warns Infostealer Malware Is Hijacking Claude Sessions
items.summary: Anthropic disclosed that common infostealer malware, including Vidar, Lumma, StealC, RedLine and Acreed on Windows and Atomic Stealer on macOS, is quietly copying locally saved Claude login sessions, cookies and credentials from infected machines, letting attackers hijack accounts and burn through victims' usage limits. The company began signing out affected users, removing saved payment methods and refunding unauthorized charges, but stressed the malware has nothing to do with Claude itself or anything users did inside it. Signing out stops the specific stolen session, not the underlying infection, so anyone still infected can simply be robbed again on their next login.

items.headline: Nvidia in Talks to Invest in Perplexity at Over $30 Billion Valuation
items.summary: Nvidia is discussing an equity investment in Perplexity as part of a new funding round that would value the AI search startup at more than $30 billion, according to The Information, a jump of over 50 percent from the roughly $20 billion valuation it closed about a year ago. The talks come as Perplexity's annualized revenue has reportedly climbed past $750 million, up from under $250 million at the start of the year, and as commercial ties between the two companies deepen. Neither company has confirmed a deal, but it would be Nvidia's latest move toward becoming a financial backer, not just a chip supplier, to the AI companies building on its hardware.

items.headline: California Lawmakers Strike Deal to Exempt Indie Films From Tax Credit Cap
items.summary: California legislators reached a compromise on a budget bill that fully exempts independent film credits, about 10 percent of the state's $750 million production incentive program, from a new $5 million-per-year cap on corporate tax credits, after the Motion Picture Association and entertainment unions warned the cap threatened the incentive program itself. The deal also speeds up cash refunds for productions that opt for one, cutting the payout window from five years to two and lowering the discount taken from 10 percent to 5 percent, while extending the expiration of older non-refundable credits by up to five years. It's a concrete win for an industry pushing back against a budget measure that would have squeezed production financing just as California competes harder for shoots against other states and countries.

items.headline: Anne Hathaway Joins Tom Cruise in Days of Thunder 2
items.summary: Anne Hathaway will co-star opposite Tom Cruise in Days of Thunder 2, playing a race team owner and engineer to Cruise's returning driver Cole Trickle, with Jonathan Levine directing from a script by Will Staples and Jerry Bruckheimer producing alongside Cruise. The sequel to the 1990 NASCAR drama is set for a June 2028 release and will be shot for Imax, continuing Cruise's pattern of betting big-budget original-feeling spectacle on theatrical exclusivity rather than streaming. It's a notable studio wager that nostalgia-driven legacy sequels, one of the few reliably bankable bets left, can still open big two years out.

items.headline: Meta's $18 Billion Settlement Puts TikTok and YouTube on Notice
items.summary: Days after agreeing to pay up to $18 billion and adopt sweeping teen-safety changes, including two-hour daily limits only a parent can lift, disabled cosmetic-surgery filters and a night mode, Meta is now publicly pressuring TikTok and YouTube to match those restrictions, taking out newspaper ads and posting an open letter urging rivals to "join us in supporting teens." Attention in the broader wave of state lawsuits over youth social media harm is shifting to TikTok, YouTube and Snap, which face the same legal exposure without having settled. It's an unusual dynamic: a company using its own regulatory defeat as leverage to box in competitors who haven't lost yet.

items.headline: Large Study Links Heavy Remote Work to Rising Loneliness
items.summary: A study published in the journal Science, analyzing survey data from more than half a million American workers between 2011 and 2024, found that people working remotely more than three days a week spend significantly more time completely alone and are far more likely to go entire days without any in-person social contact, without making up the difference by socializing more in the evenings. Working from home one or two days a week showed no such effect, suggesting the harm is concentrated among the most remote-heavy arrangements, and the researchers found no evidence that simply returning to the office reverses the isolation once it sets in. It complicates the return-to-office debate: the variable that matters most may be dose, not location.

items.headline: Kate Spade Names Jonathan Saunders Executive Creative Director
items.summary: Kate Spade New York appointed Jonathan Saunders, previously chief creative officer at H&M-owned & Other Stories and a veteran of Alexander McQueen, Calvin Klein and Diane von Furstenberg, as executive creative director, giving the Tapestry-owned brand a single creative leader for the first time in nearly five years. Saunders will oversee product design and visual identity and reports directly to brand president and CEO Eva Erdmann, taking over at a moment when Kate Spade's revenue has been sliding even as sibling brand Coach drives most of Tapestry's growth. The hire is a bet that centralized creative direction, the model most of its luxury peers never abandoned, can help reverse a multi-year slide.

items.headline: Camus's Philosophy of the Absurd
items.summary: Albert Camus argued that the human condition is defined by an unresolvable collision between our deep need for meaning and a universe that offers none, a confrontation he called "the absurd." Rather than escaping this through suicide, literal or philosophical, via religious or ideological leaps of faith, Camus insisted the only honest response is to keep living in full awareness of the absurd, an idea he illustrated through the myth of Sisyphus, condemned to push a boulder uphill forever, whom Camus imagines as ultimately happy in the act itself. The idea still resonates as a model for building purpose or commitment without appeal to cosmic guarantees, which is roughly the position many people feel they're in today, minus the mythology.
